tweet.text:
⚙️ LLM serving research

Sreetama Sarkar and colleagues from USC, UC Irvine and Intel Labs report a way to reuse a small model’s context cache when handing a request to a larger model in the same family.

RaReCache maps the cached representations, then selects positions for the larger model to process again. This targets prefill, the initial processing of a prompt.
→ Qwen3-0.6B→14B, with 30% of positions recomputed: 90.2% GSM8K accuracy versus 95.1% for native 14B processing, across 1,319 questions
→ The same setting reaches 61.2% on MMLU-Redux versus 78.6% for the target, so “95–99% retained” does not apply across all benchmarks
→ An A100 serving test raises prefill capacity about 1.8×. Near baseline saturation, median first-token latency falls from 870ms to 173ms; under light traffic, it rises from 51ms to 95ms

The timing assumes the small model’s cache already exists and uses a PyTorch eager-mode baseline, not an optimized production server. Code is promised after publication.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11358v1
